191: ✦At this point babies are about 37.6 cm long and weigh about 1,005 g.✦This is considered an important week for babies.✦Research shows babies born in these weeks have a very good chance of survival.
192: ✦Although a baby is expected to weigh 1,100 to 1,300 grams now, every baby develops differently.✦These numbers are averages; a heavier or lighter baby doesn't mean there's a problem.✦What matters is that your doctor sees no issue in the growth curve.
193: ✦The surface of the baby's developing brain used to be smooth.✦Now the characteristic grooves and folds form on its surface.✦The amount of brain tissue also increases.
194: ✦This week fat keeps building up under the skin.✦So the baby no longer looks as thin and is starting to fill out.✦The eyebrows and eyelashes form and the baby can now blink those tiny eyes.✦So this week's skill is blinking! Coughing, sucking, hiccupping and breathing movements are on the list too.
195: ✦It's very common to ask about the baby's position at this stage.✦It's impossible to tell the position just by touching the belly.✦The baby changes position throughout pregnancy.✦In the last trimester the head is most likely to be down, but your doctor will give the most accurate information during an ultrasound.
196: ✦This week fat under the baby's skin is building up faster.✦Fat will keep building up until birth and your baby will look adorable.✦Fat is also forming around the organs.
197: ✦The baby's body systems are working wonderfully.✦The lungs are close to finishing the development needed to breathe in the outside world.✦If born early after this week, babies have a chance of survival, though they need medical help.
198: ✦Your baby is about 39–40 cm long, the size of a pumpkin.✦It weighs about 1,200 grams.
199: ✦With the first 6 months behind you, you must be feeling relieved.✦It's natural to feel impatient as the birth gets closer.✦Even if your baby is born early during these last 3 months, the chance of survival is high.✦Try to stay relaxed – about 90% of babies are born at or near term.
200: ✦Most of the small airways (bronchioles) in the lungs are in place and the number of tiny air sacs (alveoli) has increased.✦Surfactant, which lowers surface tension inside the air sacs, keeps forming.✦Its production will be complete around week 35.✦As the lungs develop, the baby keeps breathing rhythmically to prepare for life after birth.
201: ✦Your baby keeps sucking their finger, strengthening the sucking muscles.✦The facial muscles' ability to breastfeed will be complete around weeks 35–36.
202: ✦This week the skin is pink and wrinkled.✦Fat under the skin is increasing.✦The part of the brain related to intelligence and temperament keeps developing.✦Reactions to different sounds, foods and light are more deliberate.
203: ✦Red blood cells are developing in the bones.✦Even as the bones harden this week, they stay flexible.✦This flexibility continues after birth.✦The bones fully harden during childhood.✦The skull bones are soft too.✦After all, the bones need to be flexible for the baby to pass through the birth canal.✦The soft spots on the baby's skull, called fontanelles, close and harden within about 1–1.5 years after birth.
204: ✦You've probably noticed the movement in your belly continues.✦There's even a rhythm and pattern to it.✦For example, the baby may be more active after you eat or when you rest.✦But if you notice the movements break from this pattern, don't hesitate to call your doctor.
205: ✦This week your baby is about 40–41 cm long, the size of a cabbage.✦It weighs about 1,400 grams.
206: ✦Your baby will gain about half a kilo every week.✦As fat under the skin increases, the fine lanugo hair that helped regulate temperature keeps falling out.✦Temperature control will now mostly be the job of the fat tissue.
207: ✦This week your baby's senses are very developed.✦They can tell your voice from your partner's.✦They can react to different tastes and bright light through your belly.✦If you gently press toward your baby on your belly, they may first pull back and then push back in response.✦Having your partner do this helps their bond with the baby begin even before birth.
208: ✦The baby needs plenty of calcium, protein and iron for bones, muscles and blood cells.✦If you don't get enough of these nutrients, the baby will take them from your reserves.
209: ✦Your baby's brain is as developed as a newborn's.✦Still, brain cells keep developing.✦For brain development, being born at or near term is an advantage.
210: ✦Your baby is enjoying the journey in your belly, sleeping and waking in turns.✦Just when you think they haven't moved for hours, a small but firm kick says, 'I'm awake now.'
211: ✦As the baby's muscles get much stronger, so do the movements.✦Though they're a bit less frequent than in past weeks, strong punches, kicks and stretches can hurt.✦Some nights they may even be strong enough to wake you up.
212: ✦Your baby is about 41–42 cm long, the length of a leek.✦It weighs about 1,400 grams.
213: ✦Your baby's organs and body systems are almost fully formed.✦From now on, the biggest changes will be in length and weight.✦Weekly weight gain is about 500 grams on average.
214: ✦This week the fine lanugo hair on your baby's skin keeps disappearing quickly.✦The vernix caseosa layer, which keeps the body warm and supports the immune system, has become much thicker.
215: ✦The fingernails have fully grown; the toenails still have a way to go.✦The baby can now close and open the eyelids much better.✦The eyes' ability to see and focus is complete.✦The brain and nervous system are fully developed.✦So the baby moves more and more deliberately each day.
216: ✦This week surfactant production in the baby's lungs continues, supported by the adrenal glands.✦Each week the lungs develop further toward breathing easily in the outside world.✦Since they'll keep maturing for about 5 more weeks, babies born after 36 weeks can breathe almost without help.
217: ✦This week your baby's movements have slowed because there's less room.✦But that doesn't mean they'll stop moving.✦If your baby doesn't move for a while, tell your doctor.
218: ✦Your baby is expected to be head-down (vertex position).✦But if your baby hasn't turned yet, don't worry right away.✦At this stage 25–30% of babies are still breech.✦Your baby may still turn head-down until week 38.✦About 4% of babies are born breech.
219: ✦This week your baby is about 42–43 cm long, the size of a head of lettuce.✦It weighs about 1,700 grams.
220: ✦All organs except the lungs are fully developed and working.✦So almost all babies born at this week or later survive.✦But they will need help breathing until about week 36.
221: ✦Your baby is getting longer and the skin keeps filling out with fat.✦The toenails have mostly grown.✦The baby now spends two-thirds of the time sleeping.✦Research suggests the ability to dream starts developing from these weeks.
222: ✦The heart rate is starting to slow a little.✦Your heartbeat can affect the baby's heart too.✦So it's good to keep your days as calm as possible.
223: ✦All of your baby's organs except the lungs and digestive system are ready.✦When awake, they can do many things a newborn does.✦They can grab their feet and suck their fingers.✦The eyelashes, eyebrows and hair are now visible.✦They can make many facial expressions.
224: ✦Although space is getting tight, your baby is still active.✦With much stronger muscles now, you may feel movements as strong jabs.✦Tiny blows or stretches can sometimes hurt.✦You can now tell better whether a jab comes from a hand or a foot.✦Some babies are calm in the womb, others very active until birth.✦This activity level usually continues after birth.✦The same goes for the sleep–wake cycle.✦If your baby sleeps for long stretches in your belly, their sleep routine will probably be similar after birth.
225: ✦From this week, your doctor won't order frequent ultrasounds unless needed.✦In some countries ultrasounds are done much more often than elsewhere.✦Since possible effects on the baby haven't been fully ruled out, fewer ultrasounds are generally better; if all is well, you can ask your doctor for fewer scans.
226: ✦This week the baby gains about 225 grams on average compared with last week.✦By the big day your baby's weight may almost double.
227: ✦There's enough amniotic fluid at this stage.✦A low level of fluid isn't healthy.✦Your baby keeps breathing regularly and making breathing movements by swallowing amniotic fluid.✦But they still get most of their oxygen from the placenta.
228: ✦Brain cells are still developing.✦Brain cell development is very important for skills after birth.✦By this week, most of the fine lanugo hair that covered the baby's body has fallen out.✦The vernix caseosa layer on the skin has become quite thick and now keeps your baby warm enough.
229: ✦The baby's hair has fully grown.✦Your baby might also have no hair.✦Babies born without hair usually have relatively little until age 1, and it starts to grow after that.
230: ✦Your baby's space is getting tighter.✦So tiny but strong jabs and stretches may hurt more and more.✦You can have fun feeling their hiccups.
231: ✦This week babies keep moving their arms, legs, body and head.✦They keep sucking their thumb or other fingers to develop the sucking muscles.✦This way the facial muscles will be ready to breastfeed after birth.
232: ✦The amniotic fluid level has peaked.✦With no room for more fluid, you may be more bothered by your baby's nudges and kicks.✦That's because there's less fluid to cushion them and your baby is bigger.
233: ✦This week your baby is about 45–46 cm long, the size of a honeydew melon.✦It weighs about 2,100–2,300 grams.
234: ✦Perhaps the most striking thing this week is that your baby fully feels whatever you're doing.✦What you eat and drink, sounds from outside, your mood – everything affects them, even how much they move.
235: ✦The vernix caseosa layer on your baby's skin keeps regulating body temperature and keeping the skin moist.✦This white, paste-like coating will decrease before birth.✦It will also make it easier for the baby to pass through the birth canal.
236: ✦The lungs keep maturing and will be fully developed in 2–3 weeks. Babies born at 34 weeks can survive, but may need to stay in an incubator for 2–3 weeks to get breathing support.
237: ✦At 34 weeks the baby's brain cells keep developing. This is important for the baby's skills in the outside world! Like all the senses, memory and the ability to remember are developed.
238: ✦You keep producing antibodies to prepare your baby for the outside world.✦At this stage most babies have settled into the birth position.✦If you could see inside, you'd notice your baby's nails are long enough to reach past the fingertips.✦If it's a boy, the testicles can now be seen.
239: ✦Your baby's central nervous system and lungs keep developing and are very close to their final form.✦If you're worried about an early birth, try not to be afraid: babies born at this stage have almost completed their development and usually do very well.
240: ✦This week your baby is about 46–47 cm long, the size of a large melon.✦It weighs about 2,400 grams.
